classification.difficultyReason: Combines square and triangle areas to locate a point that bisects a composite region.

content.prompt: Each square in the diagram below has side length $4$ cm.

spec.description: Nine squares in rows of five, three and one; P at the lower left, X four square widths to its right, B above X by one side, A above X by two sides; segments PA and PB.
spec.mathematics: Congruent 4 cm squares; PX=16 cm, AX=8 cm, BX=4 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated lengths or areas are printed.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the total area of the nine squares.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the area of triangle $PAX$ and the area of triangle $PBX$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: In the figure below, find the position of point $Q$ on line interval $AB$ such that the shaded region is half the area of the nine squares.

spec.description: Same nine-square arrangement, with PA, PB and PQ. Q is illustrative between A and B. Shading consists of triangle PQX and the entire rightmost bottom square.
spec.mathematics: The shaded region is triangle PQX plus one 4 cm square.
spec.answerVisibility: Q has no numerical position or answer annotation.

answer.short:
$QB=3$ cm, so $AQ=1$ cm.

Subtract the rightmost square from half the total area, then use the area of triangle $PQX$.
answer.worked:
The shaded region consists of triangle $PQX$ and the rightmost square.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{shaded}}&=144\div2=72\text{ cm}^2\\A_{PQX}&=72-16=56\text{ cm}^2\\\tfrac12\times16\times QX&=56\\QX&=56\div8=7\text{ cm}\\QB&=7-4=3\text{ cm}\\AQ&=8-7=1\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
